content: 1. Palbociclib: Avoid coadministration of palbociclib with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 2. Clarithromycin and Panobinostat: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Panobinostat significantly prolongs the QT interval, and its prescribing information advises against combining it with drugs that also prolong QTc. 3. Clarithromycin and Pazopanib: Clarithromycin increases pazopanib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. 4. Clarithromycin and Pemigatinib: Clarithromycin increases pemigatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pemigatinib dose may be resumed. 5. Clarithromycin and Perphenazine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Clarithromycin and Pexidartinib: Clarithromycin increases pexidartinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pexidartinib dose may be resumed. 7. Clarithromycin and Phenindione: Clarithromycin increases the effects of phenindione by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Clarithromycin and Pimavanserin: Clarithromycin increases pimavanserin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 9. Clarithromycin and Pirtobrutinib: Clarithromycin increases pirtobrutinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib during the use of the strong CYP3A inhibitor. After discontinuing the inhibitor for five half-lives, resume the previous pirtobrutinib dose. 10. Clarithromycin and Pitolisant: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Clarithromycin also increases pitolisant levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 11. Clarithromycin and Pomalidomide: Clarithromycin increases pomalidomide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 12. Clarithromycin and Ponatinib: Clarithromycin increases ponatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the ponatinib starting dose to 30 mg daily. 13. Clarithromycin and Ponesimod: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Clarithromycin and Pralsetinib: Clarithromycin increases pralsetinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Clarithromycin and Prednisone: Clarithromycin increases prednisone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 16. Clarithromycin and Primaquine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Clarithromycin also increases primaquine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 17. Clarithromycin and Procainamide: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Clarithromycin and Prochlorperazine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 19. Clarithromycin and Progesterone (Intravaginal Gel, Micronized, or Natural): Clarithromycin increases progesterone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 20. Clarithromycin and Promazine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Clarithromycin and Promethazine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Clarithromycin and Propafenone: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 23. Clarithromycin and Protriptyline: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 24. Clarithromycin and Quetiapine: Clarithromycin increases quetiapine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 25. Clarithromycin and Quinidine: Clarithromycin increases quinidine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Clarithromycin and Quinupristin/Dalfopristin: This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of prolonged QTc interval. 27. Clarithromycin and Ranolazine: Clarithromycin increases ranolazine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 28. Clarithromycin and Repaglinide: Clarithromycin increases repaglinide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 29. Clarithromycin and Resmetirom: Avoid coadministration of resmetirom (an OATP1B1/3 substrate) with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors. 30. Clarithromycin and Rivaroxaban: Clarithromycin increases rivaroxaban levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration in patients with mild to moderately impaired renal function (CrCl 15–80 mL/min). 31. Clarithromycin and Romidepsin: Clarithromycin increases romidepsin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 32. Clarithromycin and Rosuvastatin: Clarithromycin increases rosuvastatin toxicity. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 33. Clarithromycin and Ruxolitinib: Clarithromycin increases ruxolitinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of ruxolitinib to 10 mg BID if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 34. Clarithromycin and Selpercatinib: Clarithromycin increases selpercatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 35. Clarithromycin and Sildenafil: Clarithromycin increases sildenafil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider reducing the sildenafil dosage. 36. Clarithromycin and Siponimod: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 37. Clarithromycin and Sirolimus: Clarithromycin increases sirolimus levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 38. Clarithromycin and Solifenacin: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 39. Clarithromycin and Sonidegib: Clarithromycin increases sonidegib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 40. Clarithromycin and Sotalol: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 41. Clarithromycin and Sparsentan: Clarithromycin increases sparsentan levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration when resuming. 42. Clarithromycin and Stiripentol: Clarithromycin increases stiripentol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 43. Clarithromycin and Sulbactam/Durlobactam: Clarithromycin increases sulbactam plasma concentrations. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 44. Clarithromycin and Sunitinib: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 45. Clarithromycin and Suvorexant: Clarithromycin increases suvorexant levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 46. Clarithromycin and Tacrolimus: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 47. Clarithromycin and Tadalafil: Clarithromycin increases tadalafil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or reduce the tadalafil dose. 48. Clarithromycin and Talazoparib: Clarithromycin increases talazoparib levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 49. Clarithromycin and Tamsulosin: Clarithromycin increases tamsulosin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 50. Clarithromycin and Tazemetostat: Clarithromycin increases tazemetostat levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors.
